title: 1974 AHSME Problem 3
statement: The coefficient of \(x^7\) in the polynomial expansion of \[ (1+2x-x^2)^4 \] is

solutions.text:
The only way four selected terms can have total degree \(7\) is to choose \(2x\) once and \(-x^2\) three times. There are \(4\) choices for the first factor, so the coefficient is \[ 4(2)(-1)^3=-8. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: A degree-\(7\) term must select degrees \(2,\) \(2,\) \(2,\) \(1\) from the four factors
Choose which factor contributes \(2x\); the other three contribute \(-x^2\)
